chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A servant is not able to leave a successor among his people in his absence better than two Rak'at Salat. He should be saying,'

'O Allah! I Entrust myself with You, and my family, and my wealth, and my Religion, and my world, and my Hereafter, and my entrustment, and the accomplishment of my deeds', except that Allah would Give him whatever he asks for'.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer for a Muslim to recite before traveling?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual preparation for travel by entrusting one's entire being—self, family, wealth, and faith—to Allah through a concise two-rak'ah prayer. It underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating divine reliance (tawakkul) with practical action, promising that sincere supplication ensures the fulfillment of one's needs. This practice reflects the broader Islamic tradition of seeking protection and blessing before embarking on journeys.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nowfaly, from Al-Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘A servant (of Allah) is not able to leave a successor among his people in his absence better than two Rak’at Salāt.

He should be saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! 
I Entrust myself with You<sup>azwj</sup>, and my family, and my wealth, and my Religion, and my world, and my Hereafter, and my entrustment, and the accomplishment of my deeds’, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Give him whatever he asks for’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy, from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: ”Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘A servant (of Allah) is not able to leave a successor among his people in his absence better than two Rak‘at Salah (prayer). It is a Salah (prayer) that he performs when leaving for a journey. He should say, “O Allah, I leave myself, my family, my properties, my religion, my worldly affairs, the affairs of my next life, my trust and the consequences of my deeds in your trust.” He (Allah) grants him what he has asked.’”
